task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
The teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes / initiations / same-position minutes) is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=148; 148 spells; 11 cases

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: Is the teammate chosen by each pre-registered selector the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types more often than chance?
Does profile similarity add anything beyond raw opportunity (minutes, initiations)?
How many independent cases exist, given 148 spells nested in 11 cases?
How can the largest gainer be defined without regression-to-the-mean and selection artifacts?
Which placebo (pseudo-absence) baseline is needed to attribute gains to the absence?

historical_evidence.finding: Portability confirmatory T1 about movers' displacement signatures across franchises. Median Delta=+0.0557 over profile-matched decoys (perm p=0.0050), and all three decision-rule bars were met. [prior work] lists PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE as a risk.
Feasibility gate for the portability study passed (about 294-296 movers). [prior work] notes that the mover count and vacuity rho changed between the preregistration record and the final output.

Within-game adaptation toward counter play types showed an apparent PPP advantage of about +0.05 for adapters. [prior work] links this to [prior work], and the visible snippet says the no-signal baseline was the highest dPPP (full text cut).

Within-scheme re-test controlling early-PPP selection gave mixed results (DROP and HELP gaps positive, SWITCH not). Carryover gaps were not significant for DROP, and the failure mechanism was recorded as unclear.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Naive comparison of the group that shifted (adapters) against the group that did not, as evidence of a causal benefit
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as an artifact and limited by selection or regression to the mean. A no-signal baseline reproduced the lift.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Within-scheme and within-quintile re-test of the adaptation effect
failed_approaches.why: Inconclusive. The failure mechanism is recorded as unclear, and the effect was not consistent across schemes or in carryover.

evidence_establishes: Earlier project work shows that comparisons against profile-matched decoys or no-signal baselines can be run (FAM:[prior work], [prior work][prior work]).
Earlier project work shows that selection-based group comparisons can produce artifacts that a baseline reproduces (FAM:[prior work]).
Preregistered figures can shift between the prereg record and the final output ([prior work][prior work]).
evidence_does_not_establish: Nothing retrieved addresses absence spells, teammate absorption of an absent player's play types, or any largest-gainer selector. No retrieved record answers this question.
The retrieved studies concern movers between franchises and within-game scheme adaptation, so their effect sizes do not transfer to this question.
Whether profile similarity beats minutes or initiations as a predictor of the largest gainer is not established.
own_inferences: The 'largest gainer' is a maximum over roughly 7-10 noisy teammate gains, so it is vulnerable to regression to the mean and noise-driven selection, as in the [prior work] pattern.
Teammates with the most minutes or initiations have more opportunity to gain in absolute terms, so a mechanical advantage is expected. Absolute gains should be separated from share-based gains.
Profile similarity is probably correlated with minutes and initiations, so a hit for the similar teammate may only reflect opportunity.
With 11 cases, the effective sample is close to 11 rather than 148, because spells within a case share the same absent player, roster and system.
Four selectors compete for the same outcome, which creates a multiplicity problem.
uncertainties: Definitions of 'primary types', 'spell' and 'case' are not given.
The number of eligible teammates per spell is unknown, so the chance hit rate is unknown.
The 148 spells are unevenly distributed across the 11 cases.
The share of spells with a stable pre-absence window is unknown.
It is unclear whether concurrent lineup changes (starter swaps, other injuries) can be separated from the absence effect.

historical_effect.explanation: No retrieved record addresses the question directly. The [prior work] artifact and [prior work] inconclusive results, together with the placebo-dependence note on [prior work], pushed the decision toward proceeding only with changes: a chance and pseudo-absence baseline, an RTM-aware gainer definition, and case-level inference. The decision moved from a plain test to a constrained, mostly descriptive test.

blocking_constraints.text: There are 11 independent cases. A case-level exact binomial test needs roughly 5 of 11 hits (about 45%) against an assumed chance rate near 15%. Small or moderate selector advantages are undetectable.
Opportunity (minutes, initiations) is entangled with profile similarity, so a hit by the closest-profile teammate cannot be attributed to similarity without conditioning on opportunity.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved family tests teammate absorption of an absent player's play types. The cited records are used only for methodological lessons: selection and RTM artifacts, and the use of decoy and placebo baselines.

risks.text: 148 spells nested in 11 cases gives an effective n near 11 and wide intervals. Spell-level tests would be pseudo-replicated.
The argmax gainer is selected on noisy gains, and the null (no gain) hit rate is not uniform. The permutation or pseudo-absence null must use the same argmax rule.

High-minute or high-initiation teammates gain more in absolute terms simply because they are on court more. The selectors for minutes and initiations are partly mechanical, so absolute gains must be normalized per minute or per possession.
Coach replacement decisions, starter changes, opponent, rest and injuries to other players co-occur with the absence. Similarity and minutes are collinear.
Without pseudo-absence games (same teammates, absent player on court), a hit rate cannot be distinguished from ordinary game-to-game redistribution.
There are four selectors, several definitions of primary types and possibly several gain metrics.
Short spells and sparse possessions of the absent player's primary types give unreliable per-teammate gains.
Per-teammate play-type initiation shares from limited pre-absence possessions are noisy, so profile similarity is itself unreliable.
The profile must be computed only from games before the spell. If it includes absence-period data, the similarity selector leaks into the outcome.
Play types and initiators are derived from play-by-play, so label errors appear in both the selector and the outcome.

design.estimand: For each case, the probability that the pre-registered selector's teammate is the largest per-possession gainer, in initiation share within the absent player's primary types (the top play types covering at least 60% of his pre-absence initiations), minus the chance hit rate. Chance is taken from a within-case permutation of teammate labels and from pseudo-absence spells. Primary selector: closest pre-absence initiation profile (cosine or Jensen-Shannon similarity). Secondary selectors: most minutes, most initiations, and most same-position minutes. Also report the incremental effect of similarity with minutes held fixed.
design.unit: Case (an absent player's absence episode set) is the inferential unit, with spells nested within it. Gain is measured per teammate per spell.
design.sample: All 11 cases and 148 spells in 2022-23 to 2025-26 (regular season and playoffs). The complete 2025-26 files are used and the cut-off date is frozen. Teammate eligibility requires at least N pre-absence minutes and a minimum number of absence possessions (thresholds fixed before any analysis). Spells below minimum exposure are excluded, and the count excluded is reported.
design.power: At the case level, an exact binomial test against a chance rate of about 15% needs roughly 5 of 11 hits at alpha 0.05. Only large effects can be detected. Report the minimum detectable hit rate, and report results with case-clustered bootstrap intervals. Treat the study as exploratory or estimation-focused if the intervals are wide.
design.controls: Baseline pre-absence window of fixed length, using only prior games. Pseudo-absence spells matched on game count, team and opponent strength. Per-minute or per-possession normalization of gains. Shrinkage (empirical Bayes) of teammate gains to reduce RTM. A mixed-effects model with case random intercepts, opportunity covariates and similarity. Concurrent lineup changes (other absences, starter swaps) flagged and analyzed with and without those spells.
design.falsification: The same selector must not beat chance in pseudo-absence spells. A shuffled-profile selector must reduce the hit rate to chance. If the similarity selector wins only when minutes are not controlled, it is declared opportunity-driven. A split-half check of the pre-absence profile reliability is also run.
design.multiplicity: Only the closest-profile selector is the primary confirmatory test. The other three are secondary, adjusted by Holm correction across the family of four. Gain metric, primary-type threshold and window length are fixed in advance with no alternative specifications reported as confirmatory.
design.decision_rule: Supported if the primary selector's case-level hit rate exceeds the permutation and pseudo-absence null with a case-clustered 95% interval excluding zero, the Holm-adjusted p is below 0.05, the effect persists after controlling for minutes, and the pseudo-absence placebo shows no comparable hit rate. Rejected if the interval is within a pre-set equivalence margin and the minimum detectable effect is below it. Otherwise the result is inconclusive, which is the expected outcome given 11 cases.
design.data_version: Per-game NBA stats API files and the derived play-type possession records for 2022-23 to 2025-26 as available on 2026-11-01, with the 2025-26 regular season (complete 2026-04-13) and playoffs (complete 2026-06-21) final. Freeze [source] database snapshot and the code hash before analysis.
